channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Zimbabwe looks for global investors to back $200 million satellite project
item.description: Zimbabwe is inviting investors to participate in its latest satellite project aimed at boosting telecommunications connectivity.

item.title: U.S. mining firms strike new deals in East Africa as competition for Africa’s minerals intensifies
item.description: Burundi has signed two new mining agreements with U.S. companies as Washington deepens its economic engagement with Africa’s critical minerals sector, a region increasingly seen as vital to global supply chains for energy transition technologies.

item.title: China–Africa trade route hit with new $600 shipping surcharge for containers
item.description: Global container shipping group CMA CGM has announced a $600 peak season surcharge on cargo shipments from China to Nigeria and several West and Central African destinations, a move likely to raise the cost of imported goods across the region.

item.title: FULL LIST: 21 African nations gain visa-free access to Uganda in push for borderless travel
item.description: Uganda has officially implemented a visa-free regime for citizens of 40 countries and territories, including neighbouring Kenya and 20 other African nations, in a move designed to boost tourism, trade, and regional cooperation.

item.title: African agtech funding drops nearly 20% in 2025 to under $170 million
item.description: Investment into African agtech fell sharply in 2025, with total funding dropping nearly 20% to under $170 million and the number of deals declining by around 10%.

item.title: Canal+ blames high DStv installation costs for slow growth, rolls out AI strategy
item.description: Canal+, the French media company that recently acquired MultiChoice, says the high cost of joining the DStv platform is a major reason subscriber growth has slowed across parts of Africa.

item.title: Mauritania secures $1bn trade finance deal with Islamic Development Bank arm
item.description: Mauritania has secured a $1 billion trade finance framework agreement with the Saudi-based International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC) to support key sectors of its economy and strengthen trade capacity over the next five years.

item.title: Africa's energy giant tipped for financial boom as oil price hits $100/barrel amid Middle East crisis
item.description: Rising global oil prices are offering a fresh financial reprieve to Algeria, Africa’s largest country by landmass, as crude briefly surged past $100 a barrel amid geopolitical tensions linked to the Iran conflict.

item.title: EU funding for Rwandan forces securing Mozambique gas hub to end in May
item.description: European Union funding for Rwandan troops deployed in Mozambique to combat an Islamic State-linked insurgency is set to expire in May, and there are currently no plans to extend the support.

item.title: South Africans can now make profits from DStv as Canal+ releases fresh update
item.description: French media conglomerate Groupe Canal+ has announced plans to list its shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, opening the door for South African investors to invest in the company that now owns pay-television giant MultiChoice Group.
